statement.p: Find the mass of the solid bounded by the xy-plane, yz-plane, xz-plane, and the plane (x/3)+(y/2)+(z/6) = 1, if the density of the solid is given by \delta (x,y,z)=x + 4 y.

static.solution:
z = 6 - 2 x - 3 y. Note that the projection of this into the xy-plane is the triangular region below y = 2 - \frac{2}{3} x.
The mass of the volume is then M = \int_R \delta\,dV = \int_0^3\int_0^{2 - \frac{2}{3} x}\int_0^{6-2 x-3 y}\,x + 4 y\,dz\,dy\,dx. Integrating with respect to z, M = \int_0^3\int_0^{2 - \frac{2}{3} x} (x + 4 y)(6-2 x-3 y)\,dy\,dx so that M = \int_0^3\int_0^{2 - \frac{2}{3} x} -2 x^2 + 6 x - 3 x y - 8 x y + 24 y - 12 y^2\,dy\,dx. Then, integrating with respect to y, M = \int_0^3 (-2 x^2 + 6 x)(2 - \frac{2}{3} x) + \frac12(24 - 11 x)(2 - \frac{2}{3} x)^2 - 4 (2 - \frac{2}{3} x)^3\,dx. Expanding the these terms, we have M = \int_0^3 \frac{2}{27} x^3 + \frac{4}{3} x^2 - 10 x + 16\, dx = \frac{33}{2}.
